definitions.explanation: Food that remains uneaten after a meal. The most common usage.
Items remaining after the main selection has been taken. Can imply lesser quality or being unwanted.

examples.japanese: {残|のこ}り{物|もの}を{温|あたた}めた。
{昨日|きのう}の{残|のこ}り{物|もの}で{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}にした。
examples.english: I had yesterday's leftovers for lunch.

examples.japanese: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}の{残|のこ}り{物|もの}を{使|つか}って{何|なに}か{作|つく}ろう。
examples.english: Let's make something using the leftovers in the fridge.

examples.japanese: {残|のこ}り{物|もの}には{福|ふく}がある。
examples.english: Good things come to those who wait. (Literally: There is fortune in leftovers.)

examples.japanese: セールの{残|のこ}り{物|もの}だけど、いい{品|しな}が{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: They were just leftovers from the sale, but I found a good item.

examples.japanese: {人気|にんき}の{商品|しょうひん}はすぐ{売|う}れて、{残|のこ}り{物|もの}しかなかった。
examples.english: The popular products sold out quickly, and only the leftovers remained.

notes:
{残|のこ}り{物|もの} most commonly refers to leftover food from a meal but can also mean anything remaining after the main selection has been taken.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {残|のこ}り{物|もの}を{温|あたた}める: to heat up leftovers
- {残|のこ}り{物|もの}を{片付|かたづ}ける: to clean up/put away leftovers
- {残|のこ}り{物|もの}で{済|す}ませる: to make do with leftovers

PROVERB:
{残|のこ}り{物|もの}には{福|ふく}がある — "There is fortune in leftovers." Encourages patience, suggesting that good things come to those who don't rush to grab the first choice.

USAGE:
When referring to non-food items, {残|のこ}り{物|もの} can imply something unwanted or of lesser quality — the items nobody else picked.

RELATED WORDS:
- {残|のこ}り: remainder, what's left
- {食|た}べ{残|のこ}し: uneaten food, food waste
- {余|あま}り{物|もの}: surplus, extra items
